Here’s what the response would look like if you queried VirusTotal for subdomains of **example.org** with a limit of 10 and a continuation cursor of `abc`. Only the identifiers (and any context attributes that VirusTotal returns) are shown:

```json
{
  "related_objects": [
    { "id": "sub1.example.org" },
    { "id": "sub2.example.org" },
    { "id": "sub3.example.org" },
    { "id": "sub4.example.org" },
    { "id": "sub5.example.org" },
    { "id": "sub6.example.org" },
    { "id": "sub7.example.org" },
    { "id": "sub8.example.org" },
    { "id": "sub9.example.org" },
    { "id": "sub10.example.org" }
  ],
  "context_attributes": {
    "relationship": "subdomains",
    "limit": 10,
    "continuation_cursor": "abc"
  }
}
```

If you actually want to retrieve this data, you would make a request similar to:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/related_objects?relationship=subdomains&limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc
Authorization: Bearer my_api
```

Replace `my_api` with your real API key. The response will contain the exact IDs of the related objects.
